issues.description: Check name and metadata mismatch the PR's stated semantics, complecting two facts into one identity.
issues.detail: PR title says 'multiple network interfaces' (FAIL on >=2), but the CheckID, file path, and CHANGELOG entry all say 'single_network_interface'. The status_extended phrasing follows yet a third frame. One concept (count of NICs) is being named three different ways. Pick one identity for the fact and use it everywhere.

issues.description: GKE-vs-not policy is complected with the count check via string-prefix heuristic on instance.name.
issues.detail: The rule 'is this a GKE-managed instance' is a separate fact from 'how many NICs'. Encoding it as `name.startswith('gke-')` complects naming convention with managed-by identity and silently misclassifies renamed GKE nodes and user VMs prefixed 'gke-'. Push the GKE fact onto the Instance value (managed_by / labels) at the service layer; keep the check pure.

issues.description: MANUAL status for GKE is undocumented in metadata.json, leaving the value model incomplete.
issues.detail: The docstring lists PASS/MANUAL/FAIL but metadata.json Description/Risk only describes PASS/FAIL. A consumer reading the value-of-record (metadata) cannot reason about when MANUAL fires. Either drop MANUAL or make it an explicit, documented value in the metadata so the data is self-describing.

issues.description: Truncating network/subnetwork URLs to basename throws away identity information.
issues.detail: `interface.get('network','').split('/')[-1]` collapses a fully-qualified resource path into a bare name, complecting 'short label' with 'identity'. Two networks named 'default' in different projects become indistinguishable. Keep the full self-link as the value; derive the short name when displaying.

issues.description: Empty-interface branch is dead code masquerading as defensiveness.
issues.detail: GCE instances always have at least one networkInterface; the `else` branch returning PASS with 'has no network interfaces' encodes an impossible state and pollutes the value model. Either remove it, or make 'no interfaces' an explicit MANUAL/INFO with a real reason. Don't carry imaginary cases.

review.summary: The check itself is small and close to simple, but identity is complected: the artifact is named 'single_network_interface' while the PR, status messages, and docstring frame it as 'multiple_network_interfaces' and add an undocumented MANUAL state. The GKE carve-out is essential policy but is hidden in a name-prefix heuristic inside the check, intertwining 'managed-by' with 'NIC count' instead of pushing that fact onto the Instance value. The service-layer truncation of network/subnetwork self-links discards identity for display convenience. Decompose: one name for the concept, GKE-ness as a first-class field on Instance, full identifiers preserved, and the check stays a pure count over values.
